clue.text: A look maintained by Starmer, with British sangfroid

indicators.note: something maintained by another is held and kept up by it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Keir Starmer is the UK Prime Minister
lo, as in 'lo and behold', means look

explanation.surface: A cool, composed expression from the Labour leader, in the stiff-upper-lip British manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer became UK Prime Minister in 2024, so he is clued by his title's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name calm self-assurance and composure under pressure.

clue.text: Actor in a suit with no pattern turning up fine suit

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine, and to suit is to fit

explanation.surface: Someone in a plain suit finds a smart one that fits well.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit in the definition is a lawsuit, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff is the party who brings a lawsuit, so takes an active part in it.

clue.text: Parents mustn't have married different people

indicators.note: what mustn't be had is taken away, so a letter is removed

explanation.surface: Parents must not marry other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Others are people other than those already mentioned, distinct from them.

clue.text: During binge, sober stars pusillanimously withdraw

indicators.note: something happening during another falls within it, so the pieces sit inside

blocks.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Mid-binge, the teetotal celebrities timidly back away.
explanation.walkthrough: To bottle out is British slang for losing one's nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle out is to lose courage and back out of something, a cowardly retreat.

clue.text: Best ever performance from leftist full of goodness

indicators.note: a thing full of something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a red is a socialist or communist
cor! is a British exclamation like 'goodness!'

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist delivers an unbeatable, virtuous performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodness' reads as virtue, but it is the exclamation of surprise, 'cor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is the best result ever achieved in some activity, an all-time high mark.

clue.text: Drive back from Carlisle, perhaps heading north

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, backwards

blocks.note: the run straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Driving back from the city of Carlisle, perhaps heading up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, in the far north of England, which makes 'heading north' look like travel directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel is to force an attacker back, to drive them away.

clue.text: Singer Johnny Rotten's no. 1 covered by one of The Police – a cultivated product

indicators.note: number one means the first letter of the word
being covered by something puts it inside, under cover

explanation.surface: Johnny Rotten and The Police's Sting, punk-era musicians, linked to a farmed product.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny Rotten of the Sex Pistols and The Police band are misdirection; the singer is Johnny Cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash crop is grown to be sold for money rather than eaten by the farmer.

clue.text: Bones possibly set, with a different bit at the end?

indicators.text: with a different bit at the end
indicators.note: a different final piece means the last letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: a set may be a radio set

explanation.surface: Broken bones might be set, though with a fiddly end piece left over.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the final O of the wireless set for an I.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a bone of the forearm; radii is its plural.

clue.text: Son remains in Cambridge University to succeed

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair inside the institution that follows

blocks.note: ash is what remains after burning
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A son's ashes are kept at the English university town so that he may prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University suggests the English one, but it is MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts. SMASH IT is a slang phrase for doing something superbly.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash it is informal for performing brilliantly, so it means to triumph or do extremely well.

clue.text: TV magnate with fraudulent investing scoffed, given a sweetener

indicators.note: investing means clothing or wrapping round, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: Lord Alan Sugar, businessman and host of The Apprentice

explanation.surface: A TV tycoon caught out in a fraudulent investment eats, and is offered a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' looks financial but means wrapping around. Alan Sugar is a British tycoon from TV's The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar-coated means made more palatable, as a pill coated with sugar is sweetened.

clue.text: Computer file appended to mail for researcher

indicators.note: appended means added on after, so this piece follows the other

explanation.surface: An email attachment sent off to a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoc is a postdoctoral academic employed to carry out research after a PhD.

clue.text: Presumed crook judge ticked off loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A crooked judge is presumed to have been scolded and then lost his job.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to suppose without proof, which is to conjecture.

clue.text: Dope and beer left in building for event involving parties

indicators.note: in puts the preceding pair inside the structure word that follows

blocks.note: gen is slang for information, as is dope
an erection is a built structure

explanation.surface: Drugs and booze left in a building sounds like the morning after a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' suggests revelry, which the dope and beer reinforce, but these are political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A general election is a national vote contested by the political parties.

clue.text: See 18
Government naturally welcomes learner drivers here

indicators.note: a phrase that welcomes something takes it in, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: L as on a learner plate

explanation.surface: The government, of course, lets learner drivers practise here.
explanation.walkthrough: Learner drivers suggest cars, but drivers are golf clubs, and only 'learner' gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers are long-hitting golf clubs, used at the place where golf is played.

clue.text: Better to keep good list in a part of the index?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: to list is to lean over, or tip

explanation.surface: Is it better to keep a good list within a book's index?
explanation.walkthrough: The index is the index finger, not a book's index; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The fingertip is the end of a finger, and the index finger is one of them.

clue.text: Queen upset king breaks often shaky, special bonds

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from the bottom
something shaky is unstable, so its letters wobble into a new order
breaking into something means entering it, so one letter lands inside

explanation.surface: A queen distressed that a king breaks often-wobbly, special relationships.
explanation.definitionFit: Reef knots are square knots that bind two ropes, and so form ties or bonds.

clue.text: Regularly shout 'cheats' where politicians speechify

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: People keep heckling 'cheats!' at the places where politicians give speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: The hustings are the platform and campaign events at which election candidates address voters.

clue.text: Discouraging inaccurate activity on 13

blocks.note: off target, wide of the mark
putting is the activity on a golf course's greens

explanation.surface: A missed putt on the golf course is disheartening.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 13 is GOLF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-putting describes something that deters or repels, making one less keen.

clue.text: Check revenue, gutted by tax

indicators.note: a gutted thing has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: to tax is to strain or burden

explanation.surface: The tax authorities scrutinise revenue figures that have been hollowed out by taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, the verb sense of restrain.

clue.text: Figure holding Virginia up is Grace's partner

indicators.note: holding means having inside, so the number encloses the state
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: A statue holding up a figure of Virginia is partner to one called Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace and favour' is a British phrase for a home granted rent-free by the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'grace and favour' pairs the two words, so favour is the companion of grace.

clue.text: Hammered pale worker's failed balancing act

definitions.note: the answer is the performer of the act

indicators.note: what has failed has fallen apart, so these letters must be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk, pallid employee's attempt at keeping balance has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in worker's stands for 'is', joining the fodder to its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightrope walker is a circus performer whose turn is a feat of balance on a high wire.

clue.text: Current prince deprived of electronic stuff

indicators.note: deprived of means having something taken away

blocks.note: Prince George, eldest son of the Prince of Wales

explanation.surface: A modern young royal is banned from his gadgets and electronics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like electricity alongside 'electronic', but just means present-day.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to eat greedily, which is to gorge.

clue.text: Endless test about case of police work at the Met

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off
a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters count
about means around, so the shortened word surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: An unfinished examination of a police case, as detectives work at the Metropolitan Police.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met suggests London's police, but it is the Metropolitan Opera House in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York Metropolitan Opera stages operas, musical dramatic works.

clue.text: Articles from Germany and the UK, say, about craze

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the abbreviation is read backwards

blocks.note: der is a German definite article
an is an English indefinite article

explanation.surface: Newspaper articles from Germany and Britain discuss a passing fad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' are grammatical ones, a German one and an English one, not pieces of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To craze someone is to drive them mad, the verb sense of derange.

clue.text: Double whiskey brought in to Jacob's dwelling?

indicators.note: brought in to means put inside, so a letter is placed within the short word

blocks.note: W is whiskey in the NATO alphabet
Jacob is a breed of sheep, and sheep live in a fold

explanation.surface: A double whisky is taken into the house of Jacob, perhaps the biblical patriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob suggests the patriarch or a person, but Jacob here is the spotted sheep breed; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Twofold means double, of two parts or twice as much.

clue.text: Farage is hanging around charming companion

indicators.note: the words hang around the answer, surrounding it within their run of letters

blocks.note: the end of the surname and the next word

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage is seen loitering with an attractive companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is a British right-wing politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain and charm guests as a companion.

clue.text: Helen's lover speaking drunkenly in priest's district

indicators.note: a drunk slurs a word when saying it, so the name is heard with a slurred hiss

blocks.note: Paris of Troy, lover of Helen, with his final S slurred

explanation.surface: Paris, Helen's lover, babbling while drunk in a cleric's patch.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs S into SH, so Paris comes out with an H on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the area served by a single church and its priest.
